title: Calculating the sample size required for developing a clinical prediction model
study_context: Sample-size planning for clinical prediction-model development, primarily regression models.
population_or_data: Sample-size planning for clinical prediction-model development, primarily regression models.
main_findings: Required sample size depends on participants, outcome frequency, anticipated predictive performance and candidate parameters; a fixed events-per-variable rule is not a universal adequacy criterion.
limitations: Selected-page review only: PDF p.2, Summary points and introductory text. Text extracted and page visually checked on 2026-10-07.
Published BMJ article deposited at the University of Manchester; PDF page 1 is repository cover, article starts on PDF page 2.
Transfer to cardiac WSI MIL requires qualification.
does_not_establish: Regression sample-size formulas do not establish a neural MIL parameter limit; embedding dimensions or neural weights cannot be inserted into an events-per-variable rule to certify SMC adequacy.
relevance_to_project: Discuss sample adequacy in relation to independent participants, outcome events and model complexity.
